chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from al-ʿAbbas ibn Maʿruf, from ʿAli ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah or someone else, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, from Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAbd Allah, peace be upon them, who said:
I heard them both say: “What is between the buttocks and the glans has been excused: it is neither wiped nor washed.”
So by his saying, peace be upon him, “What is between the buttocks and the glans has been excused,” he clarified that what lies beyond that is not excused.

key_terms.عُفِيَ: has been excused or exempted from the ruling
key_terms.لَا يُغْسَلُ: it is not to be washed
key_terms.لَا يُمْسَحُ: it is not to be wiped

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about the area excused from wiping or washing in rulings of ritual purity?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning ritual purity, specifying a limited area that is excused from wiping or washing. It further clarifies, by implication, that areas outside this specified boundary are not excused and remain subject to the ruling.
